title: Prepositions that come in pairs
goal: Say where things are, where you are going, and where you come from — and set up the backbone of the whole course: Pashto prepositions come in twos, one before the noun and one after it.
bekal: use the six preposition pairs that cover almost every need
put nouns and pronouns into the oblique form
say where something is and where you are going

dialogs.title: خبرې اترې — د ښار په لور
dialogs.intro: Second morning. Najib is taking Budi around the city. They stand at the front door waiting for the car.

lines.speaker: نجیب:
lines.text: نن مونږ ښار ته ځو. تاسو چمتو یاست؟
lines.baca: nən mūẓ ṣār ta dzū. tāso chamto yāst?
lines.id: Today we're going into town. Are you ready?
lines.literal: today we city to go-we. you(pl) ready are?

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.text: هو، چمتو یم. مونږ له کوره څخه څنګه ځو؟
lines.baca: ho, chamto yəm. mūẓ lə kora tsəkha tsənga dzū?
lines.id: Yes, I'm ready. How do we get there from the house?
lines.literal: yes, ready am-I. we from house-from from how go-we?

lines.speaker: نجیب:
lines.text: په موټر کې. زما موټر په کوڅه کې ولاړ دی.
lines.baca: pə moṭar ke. zmā moṭar pə kūcha ke wlāṛ day.
lines.id: By car. My car is parked in the lane.
lines.literal: in car in. of-me car in lane in standing is.

lines.speaker: نجیب:
lines.text: د بازار سره یو ښکلی باغ دی. هلته ځو.
lines.baca: də bāzār sara yaw ṣkulay bāgh day. halta dzū.
lines.id: There's a beautiful garden near the market. That's where we're going.
lines.literal: of market with one beautiful garden is. there go-we.

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.text: له کوره تر باغه پورې څومره لار ده؟
lines.baca: lə kora tər bāgha pore tsomra lār da?
lines.id: How far is it from the house to the garden?
lines.literal: from house-from until garden-until until how-much road is?

lines.speaker: نجیب:
lines.text: شل دقیقې. په کابل کې ټرافیک ډېر دی.
lines.baca: shəl daqīqe. pə Kābəl ke ṭrāfīk ḍer day.
lines.id: Twenty minutes. The traffic in Kabul is heavy.
lines.literal: twenty minutes. in Kabul in traffic much is.

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.text: دا کتاب د چا دی؟ په موټر کې پروت دی.
lines.baca: dā kitāb də chā day? pə moṭar ke prot day.
lines.id: Whose book is this? It was lying in the car.
lines.literal: this book of whom is? in car in lying is.

lines.speaker: نجیب:
lines.text: د احمد دی. هغه یې تل زما په موټر کې پرېږدي.
lines.baca: də Ahmad day. hagha ye təl zmā pə moṭar ke preẓdī.
lines.id: It's Ahmad's. He always leaves it in my car.
lines.literal: of Ahmad is. he it always of-me in car in leaves-he.

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.id: Where do we go after the garden?

lines.speaker: نجیب:
lines.text: د ښار مینځ ته. هلته زوړ بازار دی.
lines.baca: də ṣār mīndz ta. halta zoṛ bāzār day.
lines.id: To the city center. There's an old bazaar there.
lines.literal: of city middle to. there old bazaar is.

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.text: زه د تاسو سره ځم، خو زه لار نه پېژنم.
lines.baca: zə də tāso sara dzəm, kho zə lār nə pezhanəm.
lines.id: I'll come with you, but I don't know the way.
lines.literal: I of you(pl) with go-I, but I road not know-I.

lines.speaker: نجیب:
lines.text: هېڅ پروا نه لري. زه ستاسو سره یم.
lines.baca: hets parwā nə larī. zə stāso sara yəm.
lines.literal: at-all care not has-it. I of-you(pl) with am-I.

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.text: پر مېز باندې زما موبایل پروت و. هېر مې کړ!
lines.baca: pər mez bānde zmā mobāyl prot wə. her me kṛ!
lines.id: My phone was on the table. I forgot it!
lines.literal: on table on of-me phone lying is. forgotten of-me became!

lines.speaker: نجیب:
lines.text: راځئ، کور ته بېرته ځو. لا وخت لرو.
lines.baca: rādzəy, kor ta berta dzū. lā wakht larū.
lines.id: Come on, let's go back home. We still have time.
lines.literal: come-you(pl), house to back go-we. still time have-we.

notes: This is the most important unit in the first half of the course. English uses one word in front: "in the house", "from the house", "with a friend". Pashto uses **two words that wrap around the noun**: په کور **کې** (in the house), له کوره **څخه** (from the house), د ملګري **سره** (with a friend). If one of them is missing, the sentence sounds like it has a hole in it.

Notice that the noun itself changes too. The word کور becomes **کوره** in له کوره څخه, and باغ becomes **باغه** in له باغه. This change is called the oblique form, and it appears every time a noun is wrapped in a pair of prepositions.

One pair that isn't a pair: **ته** for direction. The sentence کابل **ته** ځم means "I'm going to Kabul", and ته stands alone **after** its noun. It is the one Pashto preposition that is not a preposition but a postposition.
The phrase د چا دی؟ means "whose is it?". Notice that چا is the oblique form of څوک (who) — even a question word changes once it stands after د. The oblique form really does spread everywhere.

The sentence هېر مې کړ means "I forgot", literally "forgotten of-me became". This is a past-tense pattern whose rule arrives in unit 13; for now learn it as a single phrase, because you will need it every day.
The word بېرته means "back" and stands as an adverb, not as part of the verb. The sentence کور ته بېرته ځو is literally "house to back go-we", and the order must not be shuffled.

grammars.title: 🔴 Six preposition pairs that cover almost everything
body: Learn each pair as a single item, not as two words. If your head stores په ... کې as one shape with a hole in the middle, you will never lose half of it.
⚠️ In fast speech, Afghans often drop the front part: کور کې instead of په کور کې. What is **never** dropped is the back part. If you must choose one, choose the back one.

grammars.title: The oblique form: what changes, and when
body: Pashto nouns change shape as soon as they stand inside a pair of prepositions. The change is small and almost always the same: masculine words ending in a consonant add **ـه**, while feminine words often don't change at all.

Pronouns have their own oblique forms, and you only need to remember two: زه becomes **ما**, and ته becomes **تا**. The rest stay the same. This oblique form comes back in unit 13 with a much bigger job.

blocks.title: Six cities whose names you should know
items: The capital, **کابل** *Kābəl*, lies in a high valley between mountains, and its winters are seriously cold.
The second-largest city, **کندهار** *Kandahār*, in the south, birthplace of standard Pashto and the place where ښ is said with a curled-back tongue.
The eastern city of **جلال آباد** *Jalālābād*, warm all year round, famous for its oranges and sugarcane.
The northern city of **مزار شریف** *Mazār-e Sharīf*, famous for its Blue Mosque and the biggest Nowruz celebration in Afghanistan.
The western city of **هرات** *Harāt*, near the Iranian border, where Dari is heard far more than Pashto.
The Pakistani city of **پېښور** *Peṣāwar*, the second center of Pashto, with some ten million speakers around it.

blocks.title: ⚠️ The most common beginner mistakes
items: Dropping the back half of the pair. The sentence زه په کابل یم sounds like it has a hole; the right one is زه په کابل **کې** یم.
Using ته for where you are, not where you are going. The sentence زه کابل ته یم is wrong; ته is only for direction, so زه په کابل کې یم.
Forgetting the oblique form after له. The sentence له کور څخه sounds foreign; the right one is له **کوره** څخه.
Using سره without د in front. The standard form is د ملګري سره, although in fast speech people often just say ملګري سره.

exercises.prompt: Complete with the missing back half of the pair.
Put the word in brackets into the right oblique form.
Put the words in the right order.
items: دی / پروت / کتاب / کې / موټر / په

answers: زه په کابل کې یم. — مونږ بازار ته ځو. — هغه له کوره څخه راځي. — دا کتاب ستاسو لپاره دی. — زه د ملګري سره ځم.
زه په کابل کې یم. — مونږ بازار ته ځو. — زه د ملګري سره ځم. — کتاب په موټر کې پروت دی. — مونږ له کوره څخه ځو.
wave: Take ten things around you and say where each one is, with both halves of the pair. If even one comes out without کې at the back, start all ten again from the beginning.
